children: Basis bids for corn shipped by barge to the US Gulf Coast jumped on Friday, traders said, after an uptick in export demand.
Exporters sold 116,000 metric tons of US corn to unknown destinations for 2026/27 delivery, the US Department of Agriculture said in its daily reporting system.

South Korea's Feed Leaders Committee (FLC) bought around 65,000 metric tons of animal feed corn in a private deal earlier this week without issuing an international tender, European traders said. Some traders expected the corn to be sourced from the US Pacific Northwest.
At the Gulf, CIF corn barges loaded in October were bid at 85 cents over CBOT December corn (CZ26) futures, up 5 cents from Thursday. November corn barges traded at 96 cents over futures.
FOB export premiums for Gulf corn loaded in November were steady at around 98 cents over futures.

CIF soybean barges loaded in October were bid at 108 cents over Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) November soybean (SX26) futures, down 1 cent from Thursday. Basis bids rose earlier this week on Chinese demand.
FOB export premiums for Gulf soybeans loaded in November remained at around 120 cents over futures.
